title: Round 36 New Jersey-Connecticut state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for New Jersey and Connecticut. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type, state, returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned primary point; points are disclosed as points, never as boundaries, shorelines, lake polygons, or river centerlines.

services.usgsGeocoder: https://dashboard.waterdata.usgs.gov/service/geocoder/get/location/1.0 (term, states, include=gnis); accepted only on exact name/Type/state/county/FEATURE_ID/point agreement.
services.gnisDomesticNames: per-state DomesticNames_Text zips staged by .github/workflows/arena-gnis-fetch.yml via tools/gnis_extract.py into resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json; the CI runner downloads because sandbox egress is allowlisted.

selectionRules: Exact official name, compatible returned class/type, intended state, returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned primary point must all identify the intended feature before VERIFIED=1.
The seeded coordinate is the GNIS primary point; it is never described as a boundary, shoreline, lake polygon, or river centerline.
A state screen that returns an empty array leaves the feature unseeded in that frame; it becomes a generalized context corridor or stays undisclosed-until-screened, never forced into a row.

Duplicate same-name records are separated by the official description locator where present (Bear Mountain, batch-12/round-28 rule), else by returned class/type and county; the loser is disclosed, never merged.

Records keyed to another state (Mount Frissell -> Massachusetts; Delaware River -> Delaware) are never seeded into this state's rows; the bordering frame either seeds its own-keyed record (delaware frame) or carries context only.

Connecticut's post-2022 planning-region counties are stored exactly as returned; historical county division records are rejected as divisions, and the register records both the Geocoder county string and the stored county.

identityDecisions.candidate: High Point name collision in New Jersey (Summit 877098 Sussex vs Populated Place 877099 Ocean)
identityDecisions.decision: Seed the Sussex County Summit; the Ocean County same-name populated place is not seeded.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The populated place is not a high point; the Summit point is not the state boundary or a survey marker coordinate.

identityDecisions.candidate: Lake Hopatcong records (Lake/Reservoir 877238 Sussex vs Populated Place 876215 Morris vs census division 2806109)
identityDecisions.decision: Seed the Sussex-keyed Reservoir record (per-ID: feature code 39004, 278 m, null description) under the Lake row class used by the UI; place and division records are not seeded.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The primary point is not the shoreline; Sussex is the returned primary county although the lake spans Morris too.

identityDecisions.decision: Corridor-only in the New Jersey frame; the national screen keys the Stream record to New Castle County, Delaware (217887), which main's delaware frame seeds as a row; same-name KS/NM rivers and the NY-keyed gorge record are not seeded here.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The corridor is not a channel centerline or the Delaware state boundary.

identityDecisions.candidate: Bear Mountain in Connecticut (two Summit records: 205348 Northwest Hills 708 m with description vs 205347 southern 271 m blank)
identityDecisions.decision: Seed 205348 by its official description locator ("highest summit located within the boudaries of the State of Connecticut"); the blank-description southern twin about 66 km away is disclosed, not seeded.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The southern twin is not a duplicate rendering of the same summit; neither point is a boundary.

identityDecisions.candidate: Connecticut state high point (USGS Elevations and Distances: Mount Frissell south slope at the state line, 2,380 feet, Litchfield)
identityDecisions.decision: No Connecticut-keyed GNIS record exists for the slope or summit (Mount Frissell keys to Berkshire County, Massachusetts 607428); the CT frame instead seeds Bear Mountain, GNIS's description-identified highest Connecticut summit, and discloses the official-table high point here rather than seeding a cross-state record.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Bear Mountain's 708 m is not the official 2,380-foot south-slope figure; the MA-keyed Frissell record is not a Connecticut row.

identityDecisions.candidate: Candlewood Lake / Sleeping Giant / Mashapaug Lake CT screens
identityDecisions.decision: Candlewood returns only communities (Club, Isle, Knolls, Orchards, Pines, Point, Shores, Springs) plus a hill brook and beach — no Lakes record under either name; Sleeping Giant and Mashapaug Lake return empty arrays; none are seeded.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Absence from these screens is not a claim that the features do not exist on the ground.

identityDecisions.decision: states=CT returns the Stream record 206425 (Lower Connecticut River Valley) which this frame seeds; batch-17's NH/VT frames record corridor-only decisions because their screens return reservoir records only — both treatments coexist in their respective frames.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The CT-keyed point is not a mouth, centerline, or county boundary.

identityDecisions.candidate: Hartford and the Connecticut county rekeying
identityDecisions.decision: Store the returned planning-region counties (Capitol Planning Region etc.) exactly; reject the "(historical)" county division records that lead several city screens; per-ID for Hartford reproduces P1/GSA 0280 and the capital description.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Planning regions are not county boundaries of the pre-2022 system; the stored points are not municipal boundaries.

knownLimitations: Relief is labelled synthetic generalized morphology (no DEM claim); the Atlantic and Long Island Sound coast lines are labelled synthetic context lines, not shoreline surveys, and rectangles are never boundary masks.

The DomesticNames extract for NJ and CT is produced by the arena-gnis-fetch CI workflow (sandbox egress cannot reach the S3 staging zips); this register's row assertions are enforced against the extract once CI lands it, and the gaznames_default REST per-ID checks plus Geocoder screens are the in-sandbox evidence of record.
New Jersey's High Point carries stored gaz_elevation 548 m against the official description's 1,803 feet (549.6 m rounding); both values are preserved as returned.
Delaware and Raritan Canal is stored as a Stream row (Geocoder type Streams & Canals) rather than introducing an untokenised Canal class row in the starter register.
Point coordinates are GNIS primary points: they are not boundaries, shorelines, lake polygons, river centerlines, municipal limits, or address geocodes.
